17 Which amount of energy is not 2400 J?
A
the decrease in gravitational potential energy of a mass of 60 kg when it moves vertically
downwards through 40 m near the Earth’s surface
B
the energy transferred in 15 s by a machine of power 160 W
C
the kinetic energy of a mass of 12 kg moving at a speed of 20 m s–1
D
the work done by a gas expanding against a constant external pressure of 120 kPa when its
volume increases by 0.020 m3

hints: Notice each option uses a different energy formula: $mgh$ for the 60 kg fall, $Pt$ for the 160 W machine, $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ for the 12 kg mass, and $p\Delta V$ for the gas.
Recall $1 \text{ W} = 1 \text{ J s}^{-1}$ and $1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ N m}^{-2}$, so $Pt$ and $p\Delta V$ both give joules directly when pressure is in pascals and volume in $\text{m}^3$.
Calculate the four values and look for the one that differs by a factor of 10 from $2400 \text{ J}$, paying attention to $60 \times 40$ in the gravitational term.
walkthrough: List the governing relation for each case: $\Delta E_p = mgh$, $E = Pt$, $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$, and $W = p\Delta V$.

Check B, C and D quickly: $E = 160 \text{ W} \times 15 \text{ s} = 2400 \text{ J}$; $E_k = 0.5 \times 12 \text{ kg} \times (20 \text{ m s}^{-1})^2 = 6 \times 400 = 2400 \text{ J}$; $W = 120 \times 10^3 \text{ Pa} \times 0.020 \text{ m}^3 = 2400 \text{ J}$.
Evaluate A using $g \approx 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2}$ or $10 \text{ m s}^{-2}$: $\Delta E_p = 60 \text{ kg} \times 9.81 \text{ m s}^{-2} \times 40 \text{ m} \approx 23500 \text{ J}$.
Compare with $2400 \text{ J}$: B, C and D all equal $2400 \text{ J}$, while A is about ten times larger at about $24000 \text{ J}$.
Therefore the amount that is not $2400 \text{ J}$ is the gravitational potential energy decrease. This is option A

A.explanation: Decrease in $\Delta E_p = mg\Delta h \approx 60 \times 10 \times 40 \approx 24000 \text{ J}$, which is ten times larger than $2400 \text{ J}$.

B.explanation: Energy from power is $E = Pt = 160 \times 15 = 2400 \text{ J}$, so it is $2400 \text{ J}$.

C.explanation: Kinetic energy is $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 = 0.5 \times 12 \times 20^2 = 2400 \text{ J}$, so it is $2400 \text{ J}$.

D.explanation: Work at constant pressure is $W = p\Delta V = 120000 \times 0.020 = 2400 \text{ J}$, so it is $2400 \text{ J}$.
